regression-probe-half-life.finding: A narrow standalone contribution survives as longitudinal regression-suite maintenance. AgingBench measures how deployed agents degrade, while PACE and AutoJudger select compact informative evaluations, but the reviewed work does not directly estimate each probe's out-of-version predictive-value hazard and use that estimate to refresh, merge, or retire probes under a fixed evaluation budget. The thesis is valid only if future regressions are labeled by an independent full suite and the decay model generalizes to chronologically held-out agent versions rather than fitting the observed registry retrospectively.
regression-probe-half-life.required_action: Pre-register a chronological, version-disjoint probe-utility model whose only persistent update is the probe registry and evaluate it against recency, IRT, PACE-style selection, random retirement, and retain-all policies under an identical probe budget.

closest_work.title: Your Agents Are Aging Too: Agent Lifespan Engineering for Deployed Systems
PACE: A Proxy for Agentic Capability Evaluation

direct_collision.surviving_difference: Learn a probe-specific decay or survival model for predicting future agent regressions across chronological system versions, and use that model for persistent test-registry lifecycle decisions rather than static proxy selection or diagnosis of agent-state aging.

regression-probe-half-life.strongest_baseline: A PACE-style compact proxy suite reselected at every version using recency-weighted IRT statistics.
regression-probe-half-life.decisive_pilot: Using at least two independent chronological release streams, fit probe utilities only on early versions and compare fixed-size half-life scheduling with recency, IRT, PACE-style selection, random retirement, and retain-all subsampling for recall and AUPRC of regressions defined by a hidden full-suite evaluation on later versions.
regression-probe-half-life.stop_rule: Stop if the scheduler fails to reduce missed future regressions by at least 10% relative to the strongest equal-budget baseline on both release streams, or if its 95% confidence interval includes no improvement after chronological holdout.
unknowns: Whether the existing registry contains enough genuine agent-version transitions and independently confirmed regressions to estimate probe-specific decay.
Whether probe outcomes remain comparable after changes to models, tools, prompts, environments, and evaluators.

behavior-triggered-privilege-lease.finding: The security motivation is strong, but the current mechanism is an access-control policy rather than an identifiable learning contribution. Recent work already covers task-conditioned dynamic capability scoping, least-privilege inference, transient-failure escalation, mandatory runtime enforcement, and freshness checks on temporary authority. The remaining ICLR contribution would have to be a learned, calibrated lease-renewal controller whose persistent state changes from independent behavioral evidence across agent versions and which beats strong dynamic authorization rather than only static RBAC or prompt rules.
behavior-triggered-privilege-lease.required_action: Replace manually specified renewal and revocation rules with a learned version-conditioned lease controller trained on independent canary outcomes, and compare it against task-conditioned dynamic scoping plus commit-time reauthorization under identical permission ceilings.

direct_collision.surviving_difference: Persistent, behavior-evidence-driven updates to the duration and scope of task-specific privileges across changing agent versions, with renewal decisions evaluated on future versions rather than generated independently for each task.

behavior-triggered-privilege-lease.strongest_baseline: Task-conditioned dynamic capability scoping with role ceilings, mandatory runtime enforcement, and commit-time authority refresh.
behavior-triggered-privilege-lease.decisive_pilot: Run three chronological agent versions on held-out authorization tasks with executable utility and attack validators; permit every method the same maximum scopes and calls, and compare a learned lease controller with static least privilege, dynamic task scoping, MAC enforcement, and commit-time refresh on the safety-utility Pareto frontier.
behavior-triggered-privilege-lease.stop_rule: Stop if the learned lease policy is Pareto-dominated by task-conditioned dynamic scoping, if its attack reduction disappears when an external validator replaces model self-assessment, or if it cannot transfer to an unseen agent version and risk pattern.
unknowns: How independent success, boundary-violation, and regression evidence will be obtained without using the controlled agent as its own evaluator.
Whether the selected environments can actually issue, narrow, expire, and revoke credentials rather than merely hide tool descriptions.
Whether three agent updates provide enough transitions to learn a stable lease policy.

cross-form-capability-transfer-gap.finding: Format-dependent capability gaps and atomic-to-agentic prediction are already established. The potentially novel component is using a cross-form gap signature to choose a persistent update surface, but the proposed classification, free-generation, and tool-execution transformations are not automatically semantics-preserving: execution adds planning, state observation, API grounding, and recovery requirements. Without a canonical latent task and mechanically verified renderers, the transfer matrix will conflate response format with additional capabilities, and any routing gain will be uninterpretable.
cross-form-capability-transfer-gap.required_action: Construct task groups from canonical latent programs with mechanically verified classification, generation, and execution renderers before training any update-surface router.

direct_collision.surviving_difference: Use performance differences among mechanically equivalent task forms as model-disjoint features for selecting among no update, prompt, memory, and adapter surfaces, followed by evaluation of the persistent update on unseen task families.

cross-form-capability-transfer-gap.strongest_baseline: A PACE-style supervised router using raw per-form scores, costs, confidence, and atomic-capability probes without explicit transfer-gap features.
cross-form-capability-transfer-gap.decisive_pilot: Generate verified multi-form task groups from latent programs, train the router on one set of models and task families, and test on an unseen model and unseen families while giving every candidate update surface identical development examples, calls, tokens, and validation opportunities.
cross-form-capability-transfer-gap.stop_rule: Stop if gap features fail to reduce update-selection regret by at least 10% versus the strongest raw-score-and-cost router on both unseen models and unseen task families, or if the gain vanishes after equalizing calls and update capacity.
unknowns: Whether tool-execution versions of GSM8K and AgentBench tasks can be made semantically equivalent rather than merely topically related.
How prompt, memory, and adapter updates will be matched for effective capacity and training cost.
Whether the proposed adapter experiments fit the stated single-GPU budget across two models and three seeds.

recurrent-failure-contract-compilation.finding: The proposal is substantially covered as a combination of recent trajectory-to-skill distillation, validated text-space skill optimization, failure-derived hint extraction, and runtime behavioral contracts. Trace2Skill already consolidates broad execution experience into conflict-free transferable skills; SkillOpt performs bounded persistent edits accepted through held-out validation; Agent Behavioral Contracts supplies executable preconditions, invariants, governance rules, and recovery; and Deep Reflection Hinting distills successful and failed trajectories into reusable guidance. Adding applicability and expiry fields does not yet define a new learning objective, credit-assignment mechanism, or decisive experiment sufficient for a standalone ICLR thesis.
recurrent-failure-contract-compilation.required_action: Stop this as a standalone idea and merge expiry-aware contract validation into a broader trajectory-to-skill or behavioral-contract project.

recurrent-failure-contract-compilation.strongest_baseline: Trace2Skill consolidation followed by SkillOpt held-out acceptance and Agent Behavioral Contract runtime enforcement.
recurrent-failure-contract-compilation.decisive_pilot: Under one fixed context and rollout budget, compare the proposed compiler with the combined Trace2Skill, SkillOpt, and behavioral-contract baseline on recurrent ALFWorld and tool failures, using an external verifier and evaluating conflict rate, contract size, repeated-failure rate, and transfer to a frozen second model.
recurrent-failure-contract-compilation.stop_rule: Stop if the compiler does not significantly reduce repeated failures and rule conflicts relative to the combined baseline at equal tokens, or if its advantage disappears after matching contract length and verifier access.
unknowns: Whether the proposed contract representation is actually executable or is another natural-language skill document.
How applicability, prohibited-action, verifier, and expiry labels would be obtained independently from the model generating the contract.
What formal objective makes a contract minimal and determines when an existing reflection must be replaced rather than retained.

privilege-recovery-curriculum.finding: The persistent permission state is identifiable, but the proposed staged restoration is currently a rule-based governance loop rather than a learning contribution. Progressive trust escalation with safety interlocks already exists, while ToolPrivBench studies failure-driven privilege escalation. A defensible ICLR thesis survives only as a learned, failure-conditioned requalification policy that selects minimal probes and permission increments and transfers to unseen failure families.
privilege-recovery-curriculum.required_action: Replace the hand-coded recovery ladder with a calibrated failure-to-probe policy that predicts the smallest safe permission increment and make held-out failure-family transfer the primary evaluation.

direct_collision.surviving_difference: Failure-conditioned, stateful requalification after an imposed downgrade, using learned minimal probes to update a persistent permission state and generalizing across unseen failure families and task domains.

privilege-recovery-curriculum.strongest_baseline: Fixed progressive-trust escalation with safety interlocks, augmented by a ToolPrivBench-trained least-privilege policy.
privilege-recovery-curriculum.decisive_pilot: On sequential ToolPrivBench/AuthBench-derived episodes, compare learned requalification against fixed staged escalation, one-shot restoration, and permanent downgrade under identical probe, tool-call, token, and training budgets, while holding out one failure family and one task domain.
privilege-recovery-curriculum.stop_rule: Stop if fixed staged escalation matches or exceeds held-out task success at no higher unauthorized-action rate, or if the advantage disappears after equalizing probe calls.
unknowns: The proposal does not define an independently verifiable oracle for probe safety or minimality.
It is unclear whether the probe policy learns persistently across rounds or only spends additional inference at recovery time.
The identity and protocol of OR-Bench as cited in the proposal were not verifiable from the allowed official sources.

change-triggered-regression-exams.finding: The problem-mechanism pair is already established as predictive regression-test selection: use change features, dependency structure, and historical failures to choose a budgeted test subset. Active Evaluation Acquisition supplies modern learned subset selection for LLM evaluation, and SEAGym supplies the self-evolving-agent update and replay setting. Applying this combination to prompt, memory, skill, and workflow diffs is domain transfer rather than a standalone mechanism-level contribution.
change-triggered-regression-exams.required_action: Replace the test-selection mechanism with a causally identifiable update-to-failure model that demonstrates a transfer or coverage property unavailable to predictive test selection.

change-triggered-regression-exams.strongest_baseline: A faithful Predictive Test Selection model trained on the same agent-update diff, dependency, and historical-flip features, with the same random audit allocation.
change-triggered-regression-exams.decisive_pilot: At an identical 20% test budget, compare the proposed selector with Predictive Test Selection using exactly the same features and labels on update types and a model excluded from selector training.
change-triggered-regression-exams.stop_rule: Stop the standalone thesis if Predictive Test Selection reaches within two percentage points of regression recall at the 20% budget on both the held-out update types and the second model.
unknowns: Regression-Gated Self-Evolution was not identifiable as an official publication available by the literature cutoff.
The construction and validity of dependency graphs spanning prompts, memories, skills, and workflows are unspecified.
The proposal does not specify whether injected regressions reproduce naturally occurring update failures.

update-aware-permission-downgrade.finding: The coupling between persistent agent updates and authorization is timely and not directly closed by static access-control work. However, the current rule of downgrading after every update, running regressions, and restoring permissions is a composition of existing least-privilege enforcement, progressive trust escalation, and regression gating rather than an identifiable learning mechanism. Novelty survives only if the exact update diff predicts which permissions became unsafe and determines calibrated reauthorization.
update-aware-permission-downgrade.required_action: Introduce a calibrated update-to-permission impact model that outputs the temporary permission set and reauthorization probes and is evaluated on update operators absent from training.

closest_work.title: Safety in Self-Evolving LLM Agent Systems: Threats, Amplification, and Case Studies

direct_collision.surviving_difference: A versioned reauthorization mechanism that maps the exact persistent update diff to a temporary least-privilege state and change-conditioned re-grant probes, rather than applying static MAC or generic trust escalation.

update-aware-permission-downgrade.strongest_baseline: SEAgent-style mandatory access control followed by full post-update safety regression and fixed progressive-trust permission restoration.
update-aware-permission-downgrade.decisive_pilot: Run sequential prompt, memory, and skill updates containing hidden permission-relevant effects, then compare learned update-aware downgrade with unchanged permissions, permanent least privilege, SEAgent plus full regression, and fixed staged restoration under matched tool-call, test, and token budgets.
update-aware-permission-downgrade.stop_rule: Stop if SEAgent plus full regression matches the unauthorized-action rate and task success at the same total budget, or if the proposed safety gain is entirely explained by permanently withholding high-risk permissions.
unknowns: The cited Regression-Gated Self-Evolution and Change-Triggered Regression Exams are not independently verifiable external publications.
Official ToolPrivBench and AuthBench descriptions do not establish persistent multi-version prompt, memory, and skill update protocols.
The source of ground-truth labels connecting an update diff to affected permissions is unspecified.

delayed-regression-exams.finding: Delayed regression is already an explicit evaluation concern: SEAGym replays prior behavior after updates, and Governed Self-Improvement defines a delayed-regression measure for accepted edits. Merely retaining old probes and rerunning them later is therefore insufficiently novel. A thesis survives only as a learned, provenance-aware temporal hazard scheduler that predicts when each prior probe should be revisited and improves the cost-recall frontier over fixed replay.
delayed-regression-exams.required_action: Formalize and implement a provenance-aware time-to-regression hazard model, using transfer to held-out update orderings as the primary experiment.

direct_collision.surviving_difference: Learning a provenance-linked temporal hazard over prior probes to allocate future retests and estimate time-to-regression under interacting heterogeneous updates.

delayed-regression-exams.strongest_baseline: SEAGym-style replay after every update and fixed-period replay, each constrained to the same cumulative probe and tool-call budget.
delayed-regression-exams.decisive_pilot: Construct four-to-six-round prompt, memory, and skill update sequences with delayed interaction failures, then compare hazard-scheduled replay with commit-only testing, every-round replay, and fixed-period replay under identical cumulative calls and tokens on held-out sequence orderings.
delayed-regression-exams.stop_rule: Stop if hazard scheduling does not strictly improve regression recall or worst-round task utility over fixed-period replay at the same cumulative testing cost on unseen update orderings.
unknowns: Compositional Update Compatibility and Regression-Gated Self-Evolution were not identifiable as official publications available by the cutoff.
The proposal does not specify a natural source or independent oracle for delayed-trigger failures.
It is unclear whether four-to-six update rounds provide enough observations to identify a calibrated time-to-regression distribution.

version-differential-failure-localizatio.finding: The multi-surface agent setting is useful, but the stated mechanism is predominantly delta debugging applied to Prompt, memory, skill, workflow, and module diffs. It is currently a budgeted diagnostic search procedure rather than an identifiable persistent-learning contribution. A standalone thesis survives only if localization is amortized across versions, handles interacting multi-surface faults, and yields persistent targeted repairs that transfer to unseen versions and models.
version-differential-failure-localizatio.required_action: Replace generic minimal-subset swapping with a learned budgeted intervention policy trained on prior version regressions and test it on held-out model, version, and fault compositions against delta debugging.

direct_collision.surviving_difference: Amortized, interaction-aware causal localization across heterogeneous persistent agent assets, followed by surface-restricted persistent repair and evaluation on held-out version and model transitions.

version-differential-failure-localizatio.strongest_baseline: Budget-matched ddmin-style delta debugging over the version diff, followed by exhaustive single-surface validation and rollback.
version-differential-failure-localizatio.decisive_pilot: On held-out adjacent releases containing single- and double-surface regressions, compare a learned swap policy with ddmin, log-only attribution, AgentLocate-style trajectory localization, SkillAdaptor, and full rollback under identical environment-call budgets; measure exact faulty-set recovery, calls to localization, repaired success, and regressions on previously passing tasks.
version-differential-failure-localizatio.stop_rule: Stop or merge the idea if the learned policy fails to improve exact double-fault set recovery over ddmin by at least 10 percentage points at the same call budget on the second model, or if targeted repair does not reduce collateral regressions relative to full rollback.

The intended TRACE reference is ambiguous because multiple unrelated official papers use that acronym.

model-swap-compatibility-certificate.finding: Cross-model breakage of persistent assets is important, but the core probe-profile-adapt pattern is already substantially covered for prompts and skills by PromptBridge, SkillRT/SkVM, and MASA. The proposed whole-agent certificate can remain novel only as a calibrated, asset-agnostic predictor of negative transfer and adaptation cost that generalizes to unseen target-model families and held-out asset classes; merely running small migration tests and reporting risk is evaluation, not learning.
model-swap-compatibility-certificate.required_action: Specify and train a calibrated asset-level predictor with uncertainty and abstention, then require simultaneous held-out target-family and held-out asset-class generalization.

direct_collision.surviving_difference: A calibrated certificate for a composed agent state that jointly predicts asset-level negative transfer, uncertainty, and required adaptation across prompts, memories, skills, and workflows, with transfer to unseen model families and asset types.

model-swap-compatibility-certificate.strongest_baseline: Budget-matched per-asset shadow migration using SkillRT capability profiles, PromptBridge for prompts, MASA for skills, source-model success, and semantic-similarity features.
model-swap-compatibility-certificate.decisive_pilot: Train the certificate on two source-to-target model families and three asset classes, then evaluate on an unseen target family and a held-out fourth asset class against the composite shadow-migration baseline at identical probe-call cost; measure negative-transfer recall at a fixed false-alarm rate, calibration error, avoided full migrations, and avoided rewrites.
model-swap-compatibility-certificate.stop_rule: Stop if the certificate cannot reach at least 90 percent negative-transfer recall on the unseen target family while reducing full migration trials or asset rewrites by at least 25 percent relative to the strongest budget-matched profile baseline, or if calibration error doubles under the held-out asset class.
unknowns: The representation that would place prompts, memories, skills, and workflows in one learnable compatibility space is unspecified.
The ground-truth definition of adaptation amount is unspecified and may depend strongly on the chosen rewrite algorithm.
It is unclear whether probe outcomes provide information beyond direct per-asset shadow execution once interaction and token budgets are matched.
ContinualSkillBench first appeared after the 2026-08-01 review cutoff and therefore cannot support the claimed prior-work boundary.

swap-aware-regression-localization.finding: As written, the method is a factorial backbone-by-asset ablation followed by the cheapest successful rewrite. That operation is itself the strongest diagnostic baseline, and no learned localization rule, persistent update mechanism, or out-of-loop generalization objective is defined. The skill and prompt cases are already addressed by model-aware profiling and adaptation work, while the remaining multi-asset decomposition is better used as an oracle protocol for the compatibility-certificate idea rather than as a standalone ICLR contribution.
swap-aware-regression-localization.required_action: Merge the factorial swap protocol into model-swap-compatibility-certificate as its ground-truth label generator and evaluation oracle, and discontinue this idea as a standalone method.

swap-aware-regression-localization.strongest_baseline: Exhaustive factorial execution of the source and target backbones with every original and rewritten asset configuration, followed by selection of the lowest-cost passing configuration.
swap-aware-regression-localization.decisive_pilot: On natural source-to-target model migrations, compare any proposed learned localizer with exhaustive factorial ablation under a capped call budget on held-out model pairs; measure exact attribution of backbone deficit versus asset incompatibility, calls used, repaired success, and preservation of already compatible assets.
swap-aware-regression-localization.stop_rule: Do not advance independently unless a learned localizer matches exhaustive factorial causal labels while using at most half its environment calls and produces lower post-repair regression than full rewrite on both held-out target models.
